analysis.title: GS Asia: First Light / Weekly Start #47
key_insights: TAIEX lost nearly $800bn in market cap in its largest weekly decline since 1990, and MXAP had its worst week since March 2020. Clients see the AI trade tested on positioning, public sentiment and the durability of a central commercial backstop at once.
Asia Fundamental L/S managers cut gross and net exposure after a July drawdown (-15.2%) and October (-9.4%). Net leverage is at its lowest on record, and the group is down -40bps MTD.
Median Asia L/S YTD performance is only +20bps versus a +12.4% weighted average, showing narrow returns concentrated in a few managers.

Hardware value chain unwind was broad: Taiwan AI Ecosystem basket -27% WoW, Asia AI Bottlenecks -19%, Japan Optical Network -17.5%. GS optical network baskets turned negative YTD for the first time this year.
Taiwan has shifted from ballast to anchor. Foreign net outflows total $95bn YTD, with a quarter in November and $6bn this week. GIR recently cut Taiwan to market-weight.

Taiwan retail margin balances are down nearly 50% from peak to $17bn, but 53% of Taiwanese equities (44% of ex-TSMC free float) sit below the 130% margin-call threshold. Retail is 60% of volume, so further forced unwinds are possible.
Market structure rule changes in Taiwan and new Korean measures announced Sunday night, plus higher rates, add pressure. GS expects a narrower opportunity set into year-end.

India is a relative haven because it lacks direct AI exposure. Foreign ownership is at decade lows, flows were +$5bn over three weeks, INR broke below 93 for the first time since April, and Bank Nifty rose 6% on the week.
GIR upgraded India to overweight with a Nifty target of 28,500 by end-2027, backed by mid-teen earnings growth. Valuation at 20x is the main quibble.

Desk activity fell 13% versus the 3w average, and sell skew of -586bps was the largest notional since early October. Tech selling on the desk reached an eighth consecutive week, led by memory names, with modest dip-buying of Taiwan component makers.
Hedge funds rotated: sellers of Materials and Tech, buyers of Staples and Health Care. ETF activity grew 40% WoW, and long only funds were better for sale.
Weekly EM Asia ex-China foreign flows were -$7.4bn (Taiwan -$6bn, Korea -$3.9bn, India +$2.7bn, ASEAN -$200m). YTD outflows are -$274.8bn.

sector_views.rationale: GIR lowered Taiwan to market-weight on heightened volatility and accelerating foreign outflows.
GIR upgraded India to overweight, citing falling energy prices, improving earnings, seasonality and low foreign ownership.
Crowded AI hardware baskets are unwinding sharply and risk-adjusted returns have become less attractive.

earnings_insights: GS Strategy expects Indian equities to deliver the strongest earnings growth within MXAPJ ex-Korea/Taiwan over the next two years (forecast).
GIR forecasts mid-teen earnings growth for India supporting its Nifty target (forecast).

macro_indicators.interpretation: GIR's overweight India call implies upside from current levels.
INR was the best performing EM or G10 currency over the past week and month, consistent with foreign inflows to India.
A quarter occurred in November, signaling accelerating foreign supply.

risk_factors: Further Taiwan margin-call-driven forced selling by retail.
Higher rates and changes to Asia market structure rules, including new Korean measures.
Continued unwinding of crowded AI hardware exposures.
Persistent foreign outflows from Taiwan and Korea.
India valuation at 20x could limit upside.

vol_and_positioning: Asia Fundamental L/S net leverage is at the lowest on record per GS PB data.
Short interest in Taiwan was already rising and overseas supply is accelerating.

Desk sell skew was -586bps, the largest notional since early October.
Foreign ownership of India is at decade lows.
geopolitical: Taiwan mayoral elections on Saturday are seen as an early read on the landscape ahead of the January 2028 presidential contest.

tension_points.bull_case: A persistent retail community still leans bullish and can buy dips in familiar pockets where positions are rebuilt quickly.
tension_points.bear_case: Margin balances are down nearly 50% from peak, and 53% of Taiwanese equities are below the 130% margin-call threshold, so forced selling could continue.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further margin-call-driven unwinds, given 53% of Taiwanese equities sit below the 130% threshold.
